facts.text: Commerce Township is a charter township in Oakland County that contains the village of Wolverine Lake, with the cities of Walled Lake and Wixom on its southern border.
The township was originally settled as a resort destination and has since seen a large increase in permanent residents drawn by its rural setting and recreation areas.
The Huron River runs mostly north to south through the township, which also contains numerous lakes.
Proud Lake Recreation Area, about 3,000 acres at 3500 N. Wixom Road in Commerce Township, sits on the Huron River and borders Proud Lake.
Union Lake, a 465-acre all-sports lake, lies within Commerce Township.
Named communities within the township include Commerce, Glengary, Oakley Park and Union Lake, an unincorporated community in the township's northeastern part.
The lake at Wolverine Lake was created by damming several small streams in a project completed in March 1923, and the community incorporated as a village in 1954.
The northern end of the M-5 highway is within Commerce Township.
Commerce Township Parks and Recreation hosts an annual Tree Lighting ceremony to usher in the holiday season.

Holiday Light Service designs and installs Christmas lights, commercial displays and permanent roofline lighting across the township, and handles in-season service and takedown for every seasonal display.
hub.local_context: The township holds numerous lakes, including 465-acre Union Lake, and the Huron River runs through it mostly north to south, past the roughly 3,000 acres of Proud Lake Recreation Area. It also contains the Village of Wolverine Lake, whose lake was created by damming small streams in 1923, along with named communities such as Commerce, Glengary, Oakley Park and Union Lake. Walled Lake and Wixom sit on its southern border, and the northern end of M-5 is inside the township. Each year the Parks and Recreation department ushers in the holidays with a Tree Lighting ceremony.
highlights: Displays for lake homes, planned to look finished from the road and from the water
Entrance and common-area lighting for subdivisions and associations
Permanent roofline lighting for evenings on the lake, from summer through December

christmas-light-installation.title: Christmas Light Installation in Commerce Township, MI
christmas-light-installation.meta_description: Christmas light installation for Commerce Township homes, including lake houses seen from the water. Design, install, in-season service and takedown.
christmas-light-installation.h1: Christmas Light Installation in Commerce Township, MI
christmas-light-installation.hero_sub: Lake-side and street-side displays, with trees, rooflines and entries planned together and cared for all season. Free estimates anywhere in Commerce Township.
christmas-light-installation.local_paragraph: Waterfront homes in Commerce Township are seen from two directions, the road out front and the water behind. We plan for both. The street side gets the classic treatment, with a clean roofline, a lit entry and wrapped trees along the drive. The lake side might carry its own roofline outline, a pair of wrapped shoreline trees or bistro lights over a deck, and all of it reads from the far shore on a still night. Away from the water, the township's rural setting gives a single lit evergreen or a row of wrapped trees real presence. You help shape the design, bucket-truck crews handle the height, and the display is looked after all season, then cleared away once the holidays end.
considerations: For waterfront homes, decide during the estimate how much of the display should face the lake. We walk both sides, find the power on each, and plan runs so the house looks finished from the road and from across the water.

Lakes and open fields give winter wind room to build. Lights on exposed rooflines and shoreline trees are fastened with that in mind, and if a storm works a section loose, in-season service is there to put it right.

Shoreline trees and trees out by the road can sit a long way from the nearest outlet. During the estimate we measure how far each tree sits from power you can use, so the plan is honest about which trees the display can reach.
faq: Do you serve Wolverine Lake, Union Lake and the rest of the township?

Yes. All of Commerce Township is in our service area, including the Village of Wolverine Lake and communities such as Union Lake, Commerce, Glengary and Oakley Park. Send your address and we will set up a free estimate.
Can you light trees along the shoreline?

Often, yes. It depends on the tree's height, the footing near the water and how far the tree sits from power. We check ground conditions and lift access at the shoreline during the estimate before recommending a wrap or a simpler look.

A look at the property from the road and, for lake homes, from the water side. You get a layout for the roofline, trees and shrubs you want lit, a power plan, and a written estimate covering design, installation, in-season service and takedown.

commercial-holiday-lighting.title: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Commerce Township, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.meta_description: Commercial holiday lighting for Commerce Township businesses, offices, HOA entrances and associations, designed to read from the road. Free walkthroughs.
commercial-holiday-lighting.h1: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Commerce Township, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.hero_sub: Holiday lighting for offices, retail, restaurants, subdivision entrances and association common areas across the township, designed, installed, serviced and removed by one company.
commercial-holiday-lighting.local_paragraph: Commerce Township mixes lakes, river frontage and recreation land with named communities like Commerce, Glengary, Oakley Park and Union Lake, and the northern end of M-5 lands inside the township. For a business or an association here, many people first see the property through a windshield. Commercial lighting should work at that distance: a crisp building outline, wrapped trees beside the sign, and a lit entrance monument that marks the turn. We design for the approach that matters most to you, send bucket-truck crews to install it, answer service calls through the season and take it all down afterward. The township's Parks and Recreation department holds an annual Tree Lighting to usher in the holidays, and a property that is lit by then looks ready for the season.
considerations: Built to read from the road

A display seen from a moving car needs bold, simple shapes. Outlines, wrapped trees and a lit sign area do more than fine detail at that distance, so we keep the design legible from the direction most of your visitors arrive.

A subdivision or HOA entrance is often the first lit thing a resident sees on the way home. We light monuments, entry trees and shrub beds, and one estimate can cover several entrances for the same association.

Associations and property managers usually need a written proposal before anyone can vote or sign. Our estimate lays out what gets lit, how in-season service works and how removal is handled, in plain terms a board can take up in one meeting.
faq: Do you light HOA and subdivision entrances in Commerce Township?

Yes. The township is inside our service area, and association work is part of our commercial lighting: the sign or monument, the trees and beds around it, and any common areas you want lit. We start with a free walkthrough of each entrance and the power available there.
When should an association or business book?

Early fall is a good time for a walkthrough. Commercial and HOA displays take more planning than a single home, and boards often need a meeting to approve the estimate. Starting early leaves room for that vote and the widest choice of install dates.

The full season: design, installation, in-season service and removal. The estimate lists every building, entrance and tree in the plan, so everyone signing off knows exactly what they are approving before the first light goes up.

permanent-lighting.title: Permanent Christmas Lights in Commerce Township, MI
permanent-lighting.meta_description: Permanent Christmas lights for Commerce Township homes and lake houses, with app-set colors and schedules for holidays, game days and summer nights.
permanent-lighting.h1: Permanent Lighting in Commerce Township, MI
permanent-lighting.hero_sub: Lights along the roofline year-round, run from your phone. Light the lake side for summer evenings, the street side for December, or both.
permanent-lighting.local_paragraph: Commerce Township was first settled as a resort destination, and it has since seen a large increase in permanent residents drawn by its rural setting and recreation areas. Permanent lighting suits that kind of year-round life. A discreet track under the eaves holds lights that stay up through every season, and an app sets the colors and the schedule: red, white and blue for the Fourth of July, a soft warm white for summer nights on the deck, a full Christmas scene once December comes. On a lake home, the water side of the roofline is often the one worth lighting first, since it faces the view you enjoy from the shore and the one people see from across the lake.
considerations: On a waterfront lot, the view from the lake may matter more than the view from the road. We measure both and can quote them separately in the estimate, so you decide where the track goes and whether to add the other side later.

Homes on open water or open land take more wind and weather than sheltered ones. The layout accounts for exposed corners and long runs, and we explain at the estimate how the track fastens to your particular fascia.

Light carries a long way over a lake at night. A warm white setting and a schedule that switches the outline off at an hour you choose keep the lake side pleasant for you and for the homes on the far shore. We talk through colors and timing at the estimate.
faq: Is permanent lighting worth it on a lake house?

It depends on how you use the house. If you spend summer evenings outside and host through the year, lights you can turn on from your phone get far more use than a December display. Someone who only wants lights in December is often better served by our seasonal installation.
Can the lights turn on by themselves?
Yes. You set schedules in the app, so the roofline can come on each evening, switch to a holiday scene on the days you choose and turn off at night without anyone touching a switch.
Do you install permanent lighting in Wolverine Lake?

Yes. The Village of Wolverine Lake sits inside Commerce Township, and both are in our service area. Send your address, and the free estimate will show which stretches of the roofline the track covers, lake side and street side, and spell out what the installation includes.
